note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Procedural embeddings + visual memory give full separation of perception and knowledge

nodes.name: Weights entangle knowledge
nodes.description: Standard vision systems store knowledge in weights via gradient descent, which raises concerns about interpretability, privacy and bias and makes adding or removing data difficult.

nodes.name: Visual memory separates knowledge from embeddings
nodes.description: Perception with visual memory retrieves k-nearest neighbours from a database of reference embeddings, so knowledge can be added or removed by editing the memory without retraining a classifier.

nodes.name: Embedding model still leaks real data
nodes.description: The feature embedding model in prior visual-memory work is itself trained on real data, so knowledge and perception are not fully separated and removing data from the embeddings is hard.

nodes.name: Procedural data trains the embeddings
nodes.description: The embedding model (ViT-S, DINO objective) is trained only on procedural data generated by simple code (OpenGL shaders), so all real-world data enters only through the visual memory.

nodes.name: Full compartmentalization of real data
nodes.description: Combining procedural embeddings with visual memory gives perfect control over all real-world data, enabling efficient unlearning and privacy analysis with respect to all real images.

nodes.name: Shaders KML Mixup is a stronger procedural process
nodes.description: Extracting mixing masks from Shaders images with K-Means (Shaders KML) increases diversity, and applying Mixup on top yields Shaders KML Mixup, a new state of the art among procedural processes.

nodes.name: Strong visual similarity from procedural models
nodes.description: On NIGHTS human visual similarity, the best procedural model reaches 82.4% alignment with humans, within 0.9% of a Places-trained model; white-box metrics like PSNR/SSIM barely beat chance.

nodes.name: Procedural KNN classification competitive
nodes.description: With visual memory, the best procedural model beats the Places model by 15% on Flowers102, 8% on CUB200 and 1% on Food101, and is within about 10% on ImageNet-1K.

nodes.name: Zero-shot segmentation emerges
nodes.description: Procedural models achieve zero-shot and in-context semantic segmentation, with R2 on COCO within 10% of models trained on real data.

nodes.name: Part-object dissimilarity explains the gap
nodes.description: Procedural models have never seen real objects, so visually distinct parts of one object (e.g. bike wheel centre and spokes) get dissimilar representations, causing wrong memory matches that explain the remaining gap to real-data models.

nodes.name: Unlearning and privacy are efficient
nodes.description: Unlearning is done by removing samples from the memory; privacy guarantees can be computed, with less than 0.6% of training images non-private and a roughly linear accuracy-privacy trend.

nodes.name: Handles sensitive data
nodes.description: The procedural model matches faces by appearance and expression on CelebA without training on faces, and matches or exceeds the original MedMNIST result on 7 of 10 datasets.

isolated_nodes.name: Gestalt perception absent
isolated_nodes.description: Neither real nor procedural unsupervised vision models show gestalt perception on the tested gestalt images.

isolated_nodes.name: Scaling does not overfit
isolated_nodes.description: Procedural models do not overfit as ViT size increases; higher capacity yields higher KNN accuracy on ImageNet-1K.

isolated_nodes.name: Memory costs more at inference
isolated_nodes.description: Memory-based inference scales with database size and is about twice the linear classifier's time (4 min vs 1m52s on ImageNet val), but training avoids the 4 GPU-day linear classifier cost.

structural_reasoning: Argument runs from the entanglement problem, through the procedural-embedding-plus-memory design, to empirical capability results and privacy/unlearning consequences. Peripheral analyses are isolated.
